questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Major Rock Edict XIII of Ashoka:
1. It describes the conquest of Kalinga and the king's remorse over the suffering it caused.
2. It mentions Hellenistic rulers as places where his dhamma had been taught.
3. It is found only at Kalsi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: RE XIII records the Kalinga war and Ashoka's regret, and names Greek kings such as Antiyoka (Antiochus II) as recipients of dhamma. The 14 Major Rock Edicts occur at several sites (Girnar, Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra, Kalsi, Erragudi and others), so 'only at Kalsi' is wrong.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient / Bipan Chandra, Mauryan Empire; NCERT Class 6 'Themes in Indian History' (Old)

questions.q: In which script were Ashoka's rock edicts at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra, in the north-west, written?
questions.e: Most Ashokan edicts are in Brahmi, but the two north-western sites used Kharosthi, which was written right to left and was current in Gandhara. Kandahar and Taxila also yielded Greek and Aramaic inscriptions.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I Ch 2

questions.q: In Mauryan administration, as described in Kautilya's Arthashastra, the officer in charge of the collection of revenue was the:
questions.e: The Samaharta was the chief collector of revenue, whereas the Sannidhata was the chief custodian of the treasury and storehouse. Do not mix the two: collector (Samaharta) versus keeper (Sannidhata).
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; R.S. Sharma / NCERT Ancient India
questions.h: Samaharta = Samet kar lao (gather); Sannidhata = Sandook (store)

questions.q:
Statement-I: Ashoka's policy of dhamma was not a new religious sect but an ethical code of conduct.
Statement-II: His edicts stress tolerance among sects, respect to elders, kindness to servants and non-injury to living beings, and do not prescribe any specific ritual or doctrine.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Dhamma was a set of social and moral principles meant to hold a diverse empire together. The content of the edicts (tolerance, respect, non-violence, welfare) shows why it was an ethical code and not a sect.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 6 Our Pasts I

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the rulers of the Mauryan dynasty?
questions.e: Chandragupta (founder) was followed by his son Bindusara, then Ashoka and later Dasharatha, Ashoka's grandson, who gave the Nagarjuni caves to the Ajivikas. The last Mauryan was Brihadratha.

questions.q: The Lumbini (Rummindei) pillar inscription of Ashoka is notable because it:
o: records the end of the Kalinga war and his conversion
records his visit to the birthplace of the Buddha and the remission of the tax burden on the village
announces the appointment of Dhamma Mahamattas
describes the council held at Pataliputra
questions.e: The pillar says Ashoka honoured the spot where the Buddha was born and, in respect of it, reduced the village's bhaga (share of produce) to one-eighth and exempted it from bali. The Dhamma Mahamattas are mentioned in other edicts, notably Rock Edict V.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 2

questions.q: The Sudarshana lake, repaired by the Saka ruler Rudradaman I as recorded in the Junagadh inscription, was originally constructed during the reign of Chandragupta Maurya under his provincial governor:
questions.e: The Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Rudradaman says the lake was built by Pushyagupta, Chandragupta's governor, and embellished with conduits by Tushaspa in Ashoka's time. Harishena composed the Prayaga Prashasti, which is a Gupta record.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; Nitin Singhania, Art & Culture

questions.q:
Match the following Mauryan provinces with their capitals:
Province : Capital
A. Uttarapatha : 1. Ujjain
B. Avantirashtra : 2. Taxila
C. Kalinga : 3. Suvarnagiri
D. Dakshinapatha : 4. Tosali
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Under Ashoka the north-west province had Taxila, the west had Ujjain, Kalinga was governed from Tosali (near Dhauli) and the south from Suvarnagiri. Pataliputra was the imperial capital and Magadha the core province.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chandragupta Maurya obtained territories west of the Indus from Seleucus Nicator in an agreement that included a gift of elephants.
2. The Greeks called Bindusara 'Amitrochates', understood as 'slayer of enemies'.
3. Bindusara was the grandfather of Chandragupta Maurya.
4. The last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha was killed by his commander-in-chief Pushyamitra Shunga.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct; Seleucus gave up eastern Afghan and Baluchistan areas and received 500 elephants, according to Greek sources. Statement 3 reverses the relation: Chandragupta was Bindusara's father.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 2

questions.q: In which of the following sets of Ashokan minor rock edicts does the personal name 'Ashoka' (not just Devanampiya Piyadasi) occur?
questions.e: The name Ashoka appears in the Minor Rock Edict at Maski (Karnataka) and at Gujarra (Madhya Pradesh), among a few others, which confirmed that Devanampiya Piyadasi was Ashoka. In most edicts he is called only 'Beloved of the Gods'.

questions.q: According to Kautilya's saptanga theory of the state, which one of the following is NOT one of the seven elements (prakritis)?
questions.e: The seven elements are Swami, Amatya, Janapada, Durga, Kosha, Danda and Mitra. Sangha is a Buddhist community and is not part of the list, though Arthashastra speaks of sangha as a polity elsewhere.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Megasthenes:
1. His account Indica survives only in fragments quoted by later Greek and Latin writers.
2. He was an ambassador of Seleucus Nicator at the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
3. He visited India during the reign of Ashoka.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The original Indica is lost; passages survive in Strabo, Arrian and Diodorus. Megasthenes came to Chandragupta's court after the Seleucid settlement, so he cannot belong to Ashoka's reign, which came two generations later.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 2

questions.q: The Barabar hill caves near Gaya, with polished interiors, were donated by Ashoka to the monks of which sect?
questions.e: Ashoka's inscriptions in the Barabar caves record their gift to the Ajivikas, and Dasharatha later donated the Nagarjuni caves. The polished interior is an example of the Mauryan polish tradition.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania, Art & Culture; Spectrum Ancient

questions.q: In the Mauryan agrarian economy, the term 'sita' referred to:
o: a tax levied on traders at city gates
the share of produce taken as land revenue
crown lands directly cultivated under state supervision
questions.e: Sita lands were royal agricultural lands cultivated by hired labour and slaves under the Sitadhyaksha. The ordinary land revenue was bhaga, and bali was an additional levy.

questions.q:
Consider the following peoples mentioned in Ashoka's edicts as neighbours outside his empire:
1. Cholas
2. Pandyas
3. Satavahanas
4. Keralaputras
Which of the above are correct?
questions.e: Rock Edicts II and XIII name the Cholas, Pandyas, Satiyaputras and Keralaputras (and Tamraparni, Sri Lanka) as independent southern neighbours. The Satavahanas are not named in his edicts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Shunga period:
1. The Bharhut stupa railings and gateway belong to this period.
2. The grammarian Patanjali is associated with the court of Pushyamitra Shunga.
3. The Shungas were directly succeeded by the Satavahanas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Bharhut (2nd century BCE) is a Shunga-period monument and tradition links Patanjali's Mahabhashya with Pushyamitra's sacrifices. The Shungas were followed by the Kanvas (Vasudeva Kanva), not the Satavahanas.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; Nitin Singhania, Art & Culture

questions.q: The Nasik inscription of Gautami Balashri describes her son as the destroyer of Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas. Who was he?
questions.e: Gautamiputra Satakarni revived Satavahana power in the Deccan after the Shaka-Kshatrapa pressure and his mother's Nasik record praises his victories. Satavahana kings were often named after their mothers (metronymics), a distinctive trait.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Satavahanas:
1. Their official language was Prakrit written in the Brahmi script.
2. They issued many lead coins.
3. Their coinage consisted mainly of gold dinaras.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Satavahana records are in Prakrit-Brahmi and they issued lead, potin and copper coins in plenty. The gold dinara was typical of the Kushanas and Guptas, not of the Satavahanas.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 12 Themes I

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gandhara and Mathura schools of art:
1. The Gandhara school shows Greco-Roman influence on Buddhist sculpture.
2. The Mathura school used the local spotted red sandstone and was largely indigenous in inspiration.
3. The Amaravati school developed in the Kushana kingdom of Mathura.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Gandhara art (Taxila, Peshawar) used grey schist and Hellenistic features; Mathura used spotted red sandstone. Amaravati belongs to the Krishna-Godavari region and the Satavahana-Ikshvaku patronage, not Kushana Mathura.

questions.q:
Match the Sangam-age Tamil works with their authors:
A. Silappadikaram : 1. Sittalai Sattanar
B. Manimekalai : 2. Ilango Adigal
C. Tolkappiyam : 3. Tolkappiyar
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Silappadikaram was written by the Chera prince-ascetic Ilango Adigal (the story of Kovalan and Kannagi) and Manimekalai by the Buddhist poet Sittalai Sattanar. Tolkappiyam is the early Tamil grammar by Tolkappiyar.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Dynasty : Capital or port : Emblem
1. Chera : Vanji : Bow
2. Chola : Puhar (Kaveripattinam) : Tiger
3. Pandya : Korkai : Fish
4. Chola : Madurai : Tiger
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: The Sangam kingdoms were Chera (bow, Vanji), Chola (tiger, Uraiyur/Puhar) and Pandya (fish, Madurai with Korkai as the pearl port). Madurai was the Pandya capital, not the Chola capital, so pair 4 is wrong.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 12 Themes I

questions.q:
Statement-I: Indo-Roman trade with southern India grew greatly after the first century CE.
Statement-II: Mariners learnt to use the monsoon winds to sail directly across the Arabian Sea, shortening the voyage.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Use of the monsoon (credited to the Greek pilot Hippalus) made direct voyages between the Red Sea and ports like Muziris safer and quicker, which boosted trade. The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea describes this trade.

questions.q: The Prayaga Prashasti (Allahabad Pillar inscription), which lists the conquests of Samudragupta, was composed by:
questions.e: Harishena, a minister and court poet of Samudragupta, composed it in Sanskrit on an Ashokan pillar at Kausambi (now at Prayagraj). Ravikirti wrote the Aihole inscription of Pulakeshin II and Vatsabhatti the Mandasor inscription.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chinese traveller Fa-Hien:
1. He visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II.
2. He travelled to India by the land route and returned by the sea route.
3. His travel account is called Fo-kuo-ki.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fa-Hien came overland through Central Asia in about 399 CE, stayed during Chandragupta II's time and returned via Sri Lanka and Java by sea. His record is the Fo-kuo-ki (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms).
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 12 Themes I Ch 2

questions.q: In Gupta administration, the head of a vishaya (district) was known as:
questions.e: A bhukti (province) was under an Uparika and its sub-division, the vishaya, under a Vishayapati who was helped by a district board. The Gramika headed the village.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Gupta coinage:
1. Gold coins of the Guptas were called dinaras.
2. Chandragupta II issued silver coins after conquering the Shaka-ruled western India.
3. Skandagupta was the first Gupta king to issue silver coins.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Gupta gold dinaras were abundant, and silver issues began with Chandragupta II after his western campaign against the Shakas. Skandagupta came later, so he cannot be the first.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient; NCERT Class 12 Themes I

questions.q: Which one of the following works was composed by Varahamihira?
questions.e: Varahamihira wrote Brihat Samhita and Panchasiddhantika. Aryabhatiya is by Aryabhata (499 CE), Brahmasphutasiddhanta by Brahmagupta (7th century) and Kavyadarsha by Dandin.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a brick temple of the Gupta period?
questions.e: The Bhitargaon temple (near Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh) is a Gupta brick temple. Kailasanatha at Ellora is Rashtrakuta, and the Ratha and Shore temples are Pallava.

questions.q:
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the following rulers?
1. Pushyamitra Shunga
2. Kanishka
3. Samudragupta
4. Skandagupta
questions.e: Pushyamitra (2nd century BCE) came first, Kanishka (1st-2nd century CE) next, then the Gupta kings Samudragupta (4th century) and his later successor Skandagupta (5th century).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Hunas:
1. Skandagupta repulsed an early Huna invasion of the Gupta empire.
2. Toramana's Eran inscription is engraved on a boar image.
3. Mihirakula was a staunch Buddhist who patronised monasteries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Bhitari pillar and Junagadh records credit Skandagupta with checking the Hunas; the Eran boar inscription belongs to Toramana's reign. Mihirakula was a Shaiva and is remembered as a persecutor of Buddhists.

questions.q: The Sangam Chola king traditionally credited with the victory at Venni and with building the Grand Anicut (Kallanai) on the Kaveri is:
questions.e: Karikala is the greatest of the early Cholas, victorious at Venni against the Cheras and Pandyas, and tradition ascribes the Kallanai to him. Senguttuvan was a Chera king and Rajaraja I belongs to the imperial Cholas.

questions.q: The Satavahana capital was at Pratishthana, located on the banks of which river?
questions.e: Pratishthana (modern Paithan, Maharashtra) lay on the Godavari. Later the Satavahana centre moved to Amaravati-Dhanyakataka on the Krishna.

questions.q: The Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela, a ruler of Kalinga, is located at:
questions.e: Hathigumpha is a natural cave on Udayagiri in Odisha. Dhauli and Jaugada carry Ashoka's separate Kalinga edicts, which is a common mix-up, and Khandagiri is the neighbouring hill with Jain caves.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania, Art & Culture; Spectrum Ancient

questions.q: The Nalanda mahavihara is traditionally believed to have been founded under the patronage of which Gupta king?
questions.e: Tradition and the seals found at the site connect the foundation with Kumaragupta I (Shakraditya), after which later Gupta kings and then the Palas and Harsha supported it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Fourth Buddhist Council traditionally held under Kanishka:
1. It is traditionally said to have been held in Kashmir.
2. It is credited with creating the split between Hinayana and Mahayana.
3. Vasumitra presided and Ashvaghosha was his deputy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The council, held in Kashmir (Kundalvana), under Vasumitra with Ashvaghosha, is said to have compiled commentaries on the Tripitakas. Mahayana ideas had developed before this council, which did not create the split.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Harshavardhana:
1. He was defeated by the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II on the banks of the Narmada.
2. Hiuen Tsang visited India during his reign.
3. He shifted his capital permanently from Kanauj to Thaneswar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Aihole inscription of Ravikirti records Harsha's failure against Pulakeshin II, and Hiuen Tsang stayed in his kingdom. Harsha moved the capital from Thaneswar to Kanauj, not the other way round.

questions.q: The Mahamokshaparishad, the quinquennial assembly at which Harsha distributed his wealth in charity, was held at:
questions.e: Hiuen Tsang describes Harsha's great assembly at Prayaga (confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna), held every five years. A separate religious assembly was held at Kanauj in his honour.

questions.q:
Match the following works with their authors:
A. Harshacharita : 1. Ravikirti
B. Aihole Prashasti : 2. Banabhatta
C. Mudrarakshasa : 3. Vishakhadatta
D. Kiratarjuniya : 4. Bharavi
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari, Ravikirti composed the Aihole record, Vishakhadatta the political play Mudrarakshasa and Bharavi the Kiratarjuniya.
questions.s: Nitin Singhania, Art & Culture; Spectrum Ancient

questions.q: Which ruler captured Vatapi (Badami) around 642 CE after the death of Pulakeshin II in battle with the Pallavas?
questions.e: Narasimhavarman I Mamalla avenged his father Mahendravarman I's earlier defeat and took the Chalukya capital, earning the title Vatapikonda. Rajasimha built the Shore and Kailasanatha temples much later.
questions.s: Spectrum Ancient / South India; Nitin Singhania

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Pancha Rathas at Mahabalipuram are monolithic rock-cut structures associated with the Pallavas.
2. The Shore temple at Mahabalipuram is a structural temple built under Rajasimha (Narasimhavarman II).
3. The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram was built by Rajasimha.
4. The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rathas, the Shore temple and the Kailasanatha temple are Pallava works. The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by Queen Lokamahadevi of the Chalukya king Vikramaditya II, perhaps to commemorate his victory over the Pallavas.

questions.q: The Virupaksha temple at Pattadakal was built by the queen of Vikramaditya II. What was her name?
questions.e: Lokamahadevi's Virupaksha temple (Dravida style) was inspired by the Kailasanatha at Kanchipuram. Pattadakal is a UNESCO site noted for both Nagara and Dravida temples.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Pallava period witnessed the rise of the Bhakti movement in the Tamil country.
Statement-II: The Nayanars and Alvars sang devotional hymns in Tamil, drawing people away from Buddhism and Jainism.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Shaiva Nayanars and Vaishnava Alvars popularised personal devotion through Tamil hymns, and Pallava rulers such as Mahendravarman I (after his conversion) supported it. This devotional wave reduced the influence of Jainism and Buddhism.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang:
1. He studied at Nalanda under Shilabhadra.
2. His travel account is known as Si-Yu-Ki.
3. He reached India by the sea route.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Hiuen Tsang travelled overland through Central Asia, studied at Nalanda under Shilabhadra and wrote Si-Yu-Ki, describing Harsha's reign. The sea route was taken by Fa-Hien on his return and later by I-Tsing.

questions.q: According to Banabhatta's Harshacharita, Harsha's elder brother Rajyavardhana was killed by:
questions.e: After Rajyavardhana defeated the Malwa ruler Devagupta, Shashanka, king of Gauda, killed him by treachery. This led Harsha to take the throne in about 606 CE, and Shashanka is also accused of damaging the Bodhi tree at Gaya.

questions.q:
Which one of the following is the correct chronological order?
1. Accession of Harsha
2. Defeat of Harsha by Pulakeshin II
3. Capture of Vatapi by Narasimhavarman I
4. Death of Harsha
questions.e: Harsha came to power in about 606 CE, his clash with Pulakeshin II fell in about 618-630 CE, the Pallava capture of Vatapi was around 642 CE, and Harsha died in about 647 CE.

questions.q: Which Pallava ruler, who defeated the Kalabhras and revived Pallava power at Kanchipuram, was the father of Mahendravarman I?
questions.e: Simhavishnu ended the Kalabhra period of dominance in the Tamil plains, and his son Mahendravarman I and grandson Narasimhavarman I raised the Pallavas to power. Rajasimha and Nandivarman II belong to the later 8th century.

questions.q: Which Pallava ruler, originally a Jain, was converted to Shaivism by the saint Appar (Tirunavukkarasar)?
questions.e: Mahendravarman I, who also wrote the Sanskrit farce Mattavilasa Prahasana and cut early rock temples at Mandagapattu, shifted to Shaivism under Appar. Later he patronised the Shaiva faith.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Harsha's empire was less centralised than that of the Mauryas.
Statement-II: Feudatories (samantas) retained considerable autonomy and land grants carried administrative rights.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Harsha ruled through samantas who paid tribute and supplied troops, and land grants (such as those in the Banskhera and Madhuban plates) transferred revenue and some powers to grantees. This reduced the direct reach of the king compared with the Mauryan bureaucracy.

questions.q: The Mandasor inscription credits which ruler, along with Narasimhagupta Baladitya, with the defeat of the Huna king Mihirakula?
questions.e: Yashodharman of Malwa is credited with overthrowing Mihirakula in about 528 CE. Toramana was Mihirakula's father, and Bhanugupta is known from the Eran inscription of 510 CE.

questions.q: The Kadamba dynasty, one of the earliest native dynasties of Karnataka, was founded by Mayurasharman with its capital at:
questions.e: Mayurasharman founded the Kadamba kingdom at Banavasi in the fourth century CE. Badami was the Chalukya capital, Manyakheta the Rashtrakuta capital and Kalyani the later Chalukya capital.
